A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable in full, including their appendices, equations, figures and tables. Shared authors, certification framework, worked example and Two-Moons experiments establish continuity despite the rename from BiCert to MIBP-Cert.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original Two-Moons certified-accuracy and training-runtime experiments in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original results on Two-Moons, Iris, Breast Cancer and NPHA, together with solver-complexity and architecture experiments.

M1.justification: The per-step optimization and parameter-bound relaxation remain, but v2 substantially expands the constraint formulation. Section 5.2 introduces integer constraints for categorical missing values and conditional adjacent-category perturbations, beyond v1's norm-bounded continuous inputs. Appendix C also introduces convolution and sigmoid/tanh relaxation encodings. These extend the supported method beyond its renaming.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only synthetic Two-Moons classification. V2 retains it and adds binary and three-class Iris, Breast Cancer Wisconsin, and NPHA medical survey classification. NPHA introduces categorical inputs and distinct scenarios involving missing mental-health values, missing values across features, and optimistic self-reporting.

E2.justification: The Two-Moons accuracy comparators remain FullCert and Sosnin et al. V2 additionally compares runtime against FullCert and Sosnin's IBP/CROWN variants in Appendix E.2, whereas v1 reports only its own method's runtime. BagFlip's inclusion in the new capability table is qualitative positioning, not an added empirical baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds dataset-specific evaluation splits and perturbation settings, batch-size controls, and one-epoch width/depth sweeps. NPHA introduces certification rate and describes certified accuracy conditional on certification, unlike the all-test-sample definition retained for Two-Moons. Runtime reporting changes from a ten-epoch trajectory to first-five-epoch averages; this does not establish that the retained timing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's perturbation-radius and epoch-runtime analysis, v2 adds solver-branch sensitivity to batch size and radius (Table 5), network-width and depth runtime ablations (Tables 6–7), and controlled missingness/reporting-bias case studies (Section 5.2). The detailed ten-epoch timing trajectory is removed rather than simply relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report Two-Moons means and standard deviations. However, v2 removes v1's explicit 5–10-run statement and Appendix B's ten-run, matched-seed description, referring instead to unspecified iid seeds. This reduces reporting specificity without establishing a change in the number of runs actually performed.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 report Sosnin et al.'s accuracies as 85.6%, 84.0%, 44.9% versus 83.8%, 82.3%, 69.0%, respectively; the proposed method and FullCert values remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the numerical revision. V2 adds UCI, NPHA, branching and architecture results, while replacing per-epoch timing entries with five-epoch summaries and baseline timings.

T1.justification: V1 Definition 1 restricts dataset perturbations to input norm balls with unchanged labels. V2 Definition 3.1 replaces this with a general constraint over datasets, permitting coupled inputs, labels, integer variables and global restrictions. Appendix C adds explicit activation bounds, and Section 5.3 adds reasoning about binary-decision counts and search complexity. The underlying iterative soundness argument is retained.

C1.justification: V1 centers its contribution on more precise and stable certification against poisoning. V2's abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden this to natural data errors, categorical data and structured perturbations, explicitly claiming support for threat models unavailable to prior methods. Precision and stability remain contributions, but the claimed scientific scope expands substantially.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting missingness and reporting bias to prediction robustness, and explains computational cost through activation switches and solver branching. Its discussion emphasizes practical applications and additional scalability strategies. Although computational expense remains acknowledged, v1's explicit warning that costs may be prohibitive for large models and its emphasis on smaller models are softened.

D1.justification: V2 adds an implementation repository address, Gurobi 10.0.1 and licensing information, dataset generation and split details, and baseline-preprocessing clarification concerning class separation and polynomial features. V1 already supplied architecture, learning-rate, batch-size and hardware defaults. The additional Two-Moons details are disclosures, not sufficient evidence that its underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 expands positioning from tighter bounds than existing certifiers to uniquely combining deterministic certification, continuous/categorical features and complex constraints. New Table 1 explicitly contrasts these capabilities with FullCert, Sosnin et al. and BagFlip. Optimization, health-bias and dataset references are added, while foundation-model poisoning references are removed; the basic ensemble-versus-bound taxonomy remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, formal setup, complexity discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten. BiCert/BMIP becomes MIBP-Cert/MIBP, definitions precede the worked example, an explicit contribution list is introduced, and algorithm explanations move to Appendix B. Implementation material is reorganized into Section 3.4 and Appendix D.

P2.justification: V2 adds a capability matrix, a three-part UCI table, NPHA results, branching counts and architecture/runtime tables. The original timing table is replaced by differently structured summaries and comparisons. Figure 1 is retained but resized and placed beside text; the algorithms move to the appendix and are reformatted within the new conference layout.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's narrow empirical support: real tabular and multiclass evaluations, together with explicit categorical-corruption case studies, test applicability beyond synthetic Two-Moons. Comparative runtime and architecture analyses make computational tradeoffs more assessable, while dataset details and a code location strengthen reproducibility information. These gains outweigh the loss of explicit run counts and late-epoch timing detail, although large-model scalability remains unestablished.
